description: The figure presents two pie charts comparing the distribution of correction outcomes across different error detection categories for Chinese spelling correction on the SIGHAN15 dataset. The left chart, titled “All Changes,” shows the proportion of all correction attempts: 50% are successful corrections of detected errors (P), 26% are successful corrections of errors detected with high recall (R), 14% are failed corrections of high-recall errors (RW), 4% are failed corrections of high-precision errors (PW), 5% are undetected errors that were nonetheless incorrectly modified (NW), and 1% are undetected errors that were accidentally corrected (N). The right chart, “All Errors,” reflects the distribution among all actual errors: 56% are successfully corrected high-precision errors (P), 29% are successfully corrected high-recall errors (R), 6% are failed corrections of high-recall errors (RW), 3% are failed corrections of high-precision errors (PW), 5% are undetected errors that were incorrectly modified (NW), and 1% are undetected errors that were accidentally corrected (N). The legend maps colors to categories: light green for P, dark green for PW, light yellow for R, gold for RW, light blue for N, and dark blue for NW. The charts visually emphasize the dominance of successful high-precision corrections in both overall changes and actual errors, while also highlighting the relatively small but non-negligible proportion of undetected errors that are erroneously altered.
